what: Reproducibility resolved: the kernel is stable, the sessions are not
experiment: The same tile (bn=4, bw=32, 1 warp) run 5 times inside one session, compared against the same code measured in two earlier sessions.
conclusion: 1.7% within a session against 19.4% across sessions, a 13x ratio, means the kernel is deterministic and the host is not. Every earlier disagreement in this project that I attributed to code was at least partly host variance: pass 1 vs pass 2, the 139% drift, and the 68.8 vs 54.0 gap.
what_this_means_for_the_project: 64.4 GB/s is the number to quote: median of 8 samples across 3 sessions, not any single best.
The kernel is at 83% of parity with Strata and 26% of the dense ceiling.
Projected 18.8 tok/s end to end is below Strata's 22.6, so a full decode built today would lose to the baseline.
Host variance of +/-10% must be carried on every future figure, which means single sessions cannot settle small optimisations at all.
method_adopted: Any kernel number is the median of >=5 repeats within a session and >=3 sessions, reported with both spreads. Optimisations smaller than ~10% cannot be resolved on this infrastructure and should not be claimed.
